items.text: Pakistani defence minister Khawaja Asif says that a deal between Iran and the United States is "close", including an arrangement over the Strait of Hormuz. ((Bloomberg)) ((CNBC))

The Wall Street Journal reports that a U.S. military helicopter has fired at the rudder of the Panama-flagged container ship Vela ​Nova after crews ignored the naval blockade re-imposed in July, contradicting British maritime management that it was hit by a missile in the Gulf of Oman. ((Reuters))

The Israeli Army Radio reports that the Israel Defense Forces have targeted a Hamas sniper near the Yellow Line in the Gaza Strip, its first strike on the enclave in 10 days. ((AIN)) ((The Times of Israel)) ((The Jerusalem Post))
The Pentagon tells the U.S. Congress that U.S. military strikes against Houthi rebels in Yemen in 2025 killed 153 civilians and injured another 243. ((The Hill))
The Yemeni government reports that six people have been killed in strikes on a cargo ship by the Houthis in the Bab-el-Mandeb. ((The New York Times))

A heavy attack on civilians by the Rapid Support Forces and Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North is reported in Geissan in Sudan's Blue Nile state, including on the main market, surrounding farms, and other shops. ((Sudan Tribune))
Attacks by the RSF and SPLM-N are also reported in Qaysān on its provincial headquarters and a market. ((Sudan Tribune in Arabic))
Around 60 people are killed and around 50 others injured in an armed attack during a cattle raid in Tonj North County, Warrap State, South Sudan. ((AFP via Arab News)) ((Radio Tamazuj))

The death toll from the earthquake in Colombia yesterday increases to over 240 people killed, 570 injured, and at least 3,000 others still missing. President Abelardo de la Espriella declares a national state of emergency. ((The Guardian))

Search operations for the landslide from Sunday conclude in Baguio, Philippines, placing the final death toll at 10 people killed. Meanwhile, the national police places the nationwide toll from the tropical cyclones and monsoons at 26. ((ABS-CBN News)) ((Philippine Daily Inquirer))
​At least 18 people are killed and around 30 others are injured in a two-vehicle collision in Ismailia Governorate, Egypt. ((Al Ahram))
Three people are killed following a commercial building fire in Giza, Egypt. ((Al Ahram))
Four people are killed and five others are injured after an old residential building collapses in Cairo, Egypt. ((Gulf News))

The Syrian government confirms their cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency to purge nuclear materials at a hidden facility following a report by Axios on such plan after an agreement between Israel, Syria, and the United States. Conversely, Israel threatens to bombard the site again if the materials remain, and to prevent access to the site. ((AA)) ((Axios)) ((The Jerusalem Post))

The Criminal Court in Damascus, Syria, sentences deposed president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia, and former Daraa political security director Atef Najib in person, and issue international arrest warrants for all for premeditated murder and crimes against humanity. ((AFP via The Standard)) ((The National))
Lebanon's parliament votes to abolish the death penalty. ((BBC News))
A United States Marine Corps soldier is released from Russia after having been detained there since 2022. ((Kyiv Independent))

Former Supreme Court president András Baka is elected as Hungarian president through a supermajority and is scheduled to take office on 19 August. He ran uncontested as the Tisza Party's candidate, as neither Fidesz nor its partner KNDP nominated a candidate. ((Reuters))
